thread.title: Google parent Alphabet's stock becomes 2nd FANG to produce 'death cross' and Netflix is next

author: morningstar.com
title: Google parent Alphabet's stock becomes 2nd FANG to produce 'death cross' and Netflix is next
text:
By Tomi Kilgore, MarketWatch
Alphabet shares remain above their bear-market threshold, but the other 3 FANGs have already crossed below
Google parent Alphabet Inc.'s stock chart has just produced a bearish "death cross" chart pattern for the first time in over two years, that may put the future of the internet giant's 7-year old bull market in doubt.
The stock's 50-day moving average, which chart watchers use as a guide to the short-term trend, fell to $1,129.914 on Thursday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/google-parent-alphabets-stock-set-to-produce-bearish-death-cross-pattern-at-the-open-2018-11-15) from $1,132.173 the previous session, to cross below the 200-day moving average, seen by many as a long-term trend tracker, which slipped to $1,130.032 from $1,130.585.
Some chart watchers believe the cross marks the spot when a shorter-term slump morphs into a longer-term downtrend. Although death crosses don't always provide good market-timing signals, they highlight the fact that the latest weakness is more than just a garden-variety pullback.
Don't miss: Small-cap death cross: buying opportunity or a bear-market warning signal (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/small-cap-death-cross-buying-opportunity-or-bear-market-warning-sign-2018-11-14).
The last time Alphabet's stock(GOOGL)produced a death cross was June 24, 2016. The next trading session, the stock bottomed at a correction closing low of $681.14. The stock shot up 19% over the next 3 months.
The difference between then and now, however, is that the current death cross comes as the 200-day moving average is declining, meaning the stock's weakness had already impacted the long-term trend. The death cross in 2016 appeared while the 200-day moving average was still rising.
Alphabet shares closed Thursday up 1.6%, but have shed 17% since the July 26 record close of $1,285.50. Many chart watchers believe a decline of 20% or more from a bull-market high defines a bear market. The last time the shares were in a bear market was Oct. 13, 2011.
Alphabet is now the second "FANG" stock--acronym for Facebook Inc.(FB), Amazon.com Inc.(AMZN), Netflix Inc.(NFLX)and Google--to produce a death cross, but it won't be the last. The other 3 FANGs were already in bear markets.
A bearish cross appeared in Facebook's chart on Sept. 20. The social media company's stock has fallen 13% since then, and is 34% below the July 25 record close of $217.50:
Also read: A Facebook 'death cross' has arrived, and it may actually be bearish this time (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/will-facebooks-third-ever-death-cross-be-the-charm-for-bears-2018-04-12).
For Netflix, the pattern may appear early next week. The stock's 50-day moving average was at $337.250 early Friday, and has been falling by about $1.042 a day this month, while the 200-day moving average came in at $336.186 and has been rising by about $0.236 a day.
That would suggest a death cross could appear as early as Monday. The stock has declined 31% since closing at a record $418.97 on July 9:
Meanwhile, Amazon's 50-day moving average extended to $1,806.57 early Friday, and has been falling by about $6.002 a day this month; the 200-day moving average came in at $1,688.65 and has been rising by about $1.412 a day.
Read more: Opinion: How I came to respect the 'death-cross' strategy in stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/how-i-came-to-respect-the-death-cross-strategy-in-stocks-2016-02-03).
At those rates of change, a bearish cross under could appear in about 16 sessions, or around Dec. 11. The shares have slumped 21% since closing at a record $2,039.51 on Sept. 4:
If Apple Inc.(AAPL)was included in the "FAANGs," it could be nearly 50 trading sessions before a death cross appears at current rates of change for the moving average. A bear market might appear much sooner, as the stock currently sits nearly 18% below its Oct. 3 record of $232.07.
In comparison, the S&P 500 Index's50-day moving average was at 2,812.569 early Friday, about a month away from falling below the 200-day moving average of 2,760.662 at current rates of change. The broad-market tracker was just 6.8% below its Sept. 20 record of 2,930.75.
-Tomi Kilgore; 18-18 1033ET
